summary: European residence-for-the-wealthy schemes not covered elsewhere: Malta (MRVP 2015-2021, MPRP terms over time, Global Residence Programme and its predecessor and successor), the Netherlands (investor permit 2013-2024: fewer than ten permits; closed 17 Apr 2024, not 1 Jan 2024), Switzerland (lump-sum taxation: FDK counts and revenue 2008-2018; cantonal fiscal-interest permits), Monaco, Lithuania, Estonia, Croatia, Luxembourg (9 investor titles 2018-2024, repeal bill pending) and France. Laws are well documented; official statistics are scarce. Malta publishes no Residency Malta annual report, so its numbers come from ministers' statements relayed by the press and agency data given to the trade press; gov.mt and pq.gov.mt block downloads.

events.title: Malta Residence and Visa Programme regulations published
events.description: L.N. 288 of 2015 creates the MRVP: permanent residence certificate for a EUR 30,000 contribution, EUR 250,000 qualifying investment and a qualifying property, run by Identity Malta.
events.quote: The title of these regulations is the Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations, 2015.

events.title: MRVP moved to the Malta Residence and Visa Agency; parents cost EUR 5,000 extra
events.description: L.N. 189 of 2017 replaces Identity Malta by the Malta Residence and Visa Agency, adds EUR 5,000 per parent or grandparent, and allows adding family members later against EUR 5,000 fees.
events.quote: five thousand euro (€5,000) per parent or grandparent of the main applicant or of the spouse

events.title: MRVP wound down as the MPRP is published
events.description: L.N. 122 of 2021, published with the MPRP regulations, sets deadlines for concluding pending MRVP applications (end-2021 or 31 Mar 2022) and lets applicants pay an extra EUR 38,000 or 68,000 instead of the EUR 250,000 investment.
events.quote: the applicant shall be allowed until the 31st March 2022 to conclude his application for a certificate upon payment of the additional contribution

events.title: MPRP thresholds and fees raised
events.description: L.N. 310 of 2024: property EUR 375,000 and rent EUR 14,000 everywhere (regional discounts dropped), administration fee EUR 50,000, contribution EUR 30,000 (owned) or 60,000 (rented), EUR 5,000 fee and EUR 5,000 contribution per dependant; new EUR 650,000 assets option.
events.quote: These regulations shall come into force on 1st January 2025.

events.title: MPRP fees restructured: EUR 60,000 fee and single EUR 37,000 contribution
events.description: L.N. 146 of 2025 sets a EUR 60,000 administration fee, EUR 7,500 per adult dependant, one EUR 37,000 contribution for owners and tenants, a EUR 5,000 annual agent licence fee and a one-year temporary permit while an application is processed; it applies to applications filed since 1 Jan 2025 not yet concluded.
events.quote: shall apply also to applications submitted after the 1st January 2025 which are still not concluded

events.title: Global Residence Programme starts
events.description: Global Residence Programme Rules (L.N. 167 of 2013): special tax status for non-EU nationals holding qualifying property, with a 15% tax on remitted foreign income and a EUR 15,000 minimum tax.
events.quote: These rules shall be deemed to have come into force with effect from 1st July, 2013.

events.title: High Net Worth Individuals (non-EU) scheme closes to applications
events.description: No applications under the 2011 High Net Worth Individuals - Non-EU/EEA/Swiss Nationals Rules after 30 Jun 2013; beneficiaries may switch to the GRP.
events.quote: the Commissioner shall not receive any applications for special tax status under these rules after 30th June, 2013

events.title: Individual Tax Programme Rules published, to apply from 2027
events.description: L.N. 195 of 2026 creates a single Individual Tax Programme from 1 Jan 2027 (EUR 700,000 property, EUR 14,000 rent, EUR 35,000 minimum tax for global residents, five-year renewable status); statuses granted or applied for by 31 Dec 2026 continue until 31 Dec 2031.
events.quote: any granting of special tax status made before or up to 31st December 2026, including for the avoidance of doubt, any applications for the granting of such status received up to the same date, shall continue to apply until 31st December 2031

events.title: Dutch residence scheme for wealthy foreigners (foreign investors) starts
events.description: The Modern Migration Policy decree introduces a residence permit for foreigners with at least EUR 1,250,000 (art. 3.29a Vb 2000), narrowed in policy to investment in an innovative Dutch company.
events.quote: Op 1 oktober 2013 is het Besluit modern migratiebeleid (Stb. 2010, 307) in werking getreden.

events.title: Dutch cabinet decides to abolish the investor scheme
events.description: After a one-year review announced in Nov 2019, the State Secretary tells parliament the scheme will be abolished because it cannot be adapted while keeping safeguards against abuse.

events.description: Staatsblad 2024, 83 (issued 16 Apr 2024, in force the next day) removes the wealthy-foreigner ground; the policy rules state that new applications from 17 Apr 2024 are refused, while pending applications and renewals are still handled. (Not 1 Jan 2024 as sometimes stated.)
events.quote: Het beleid voor een vreemdeling om in aanmerking te komen voor een verblijfsvergunning regulier voor bepaalde tijd als vermogende vreemdeling is per 17 april 2024 beëindigd.

events.title: Swiss federal reform of lump-sum taxation in force
events.description: The federal act of 28 Sep 2012 sets a CHF 400,000 minimum base for direct federal tax and at least seven times the rent; cantons must set a minimum too. Old-law taxpayers had five years to adapt (to 2021).
events.quote: Fassung gemäss Ziff. I 1 des BG vom 28. Sept. 2012, in Kraft seit 1. Jan. 2016

events.title: Swiss voters reject abolition of lump-sum taxation
events.description: The popular initiative "Schluss mit den Steuerprivilegien für Millionäre" is rejected with 59.2% no (turnout 49.9%); only Schaffhausen votes yes.
events.quote: Die Initiative wird mit einem Nein-Stimmenanteil von 59,2% abgelehnt.

events.title: Five cantons have abolished lump-sum taxation
events.description: By end-2018 the cantons of Zurich, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Schaffhausen and Appenzell Ausserrhoden no longer offered lump-sum taxation (Zurich by popular vote, per the 2011 Federal Council message).
events.quote: Die Kantone ZH, BS, BL, SH und AR haben die Aufwandbesteuerung abgeschafft und folglich keine Daten für 2018.

events.title: Estonia adds a residence permit for large investors (EUR 1 million)
events.description: Amendment RT I, 03.01.2017, 1 creates a temporary residence permit for enterprise for large investors with no obligation to live in Estonia.
events.quote: Temporary residence permit issued to large investor for enterprise [RT I, 03.01.2017, 1 - entry into force 18.01.2017]

events.title: Lithuania adds a EUR 260,000 investor route
events.description: Law XII-2609 (14 Sep 2016, published 19 Sep 2016) adds art. 45(1)(1¹): temporary residence for a foreigner who invested at least EUR 260,000 in a company with at least five full-time jobs. Entry-into-force date not checked.
events.quote: Papildyta straipsnio punktu: Nr. XII-2609, 2016-09-14, paskelbta TAR 2016-09-19

events.title: Luxembourg government tables bill to abolish its investor residence permit
events.description: Bill 8586 would repeal arts. 53bis-53quater (the "Golden Visa"): only 9 titles issued since 2017, none of the first 7 renewed, and checks hard to carry out. Still in committee in Sep 2026.
events.quote: le projet de loi tend à abroger le titre de séjour pour investisseur, communément désigné par « Golden Visa »

programs.name: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP)
programs.notes: Update of the existing row. Successor to the Malta Residence and Visa Programme (mlt-mrvp), created by L.N. 121 of 2021 (S.L. 217.26), run by Residency Malta Agency. Permanent residence for buying (EUR 375,000 since 2025) or renting (EUR 14,000 a year) property, plus a non-refundable contribution and administration fee, and an assets test (EUR 500,000 or 650,000). Fees raised from 1 Jan 2025 (L.N. 310/2024) and restructured in Jul 2025 (L.N. 146/2025). No annual report or official statistics published online; figures come from ministers' statements and parliamentary answers relayed by the press, and from data the agency gave to the trade press (MRVP and MPRP usually combined). Does not lead to citizenship by itself.

programs.name: Malta Residence and Visa Programme (MRVP)
programs.notes: Created by L.N. 288 of 2015 (S.L. 217.18): residence certificate entitling the holder to reside, settle or stay indefinitely in exchange for a EUR 30,000 contribution, a EUR 250,000 qualifying investment (government stocks) and a qualifying property (EUR 320,000/270,000 purchase or EUR 12,000/10,000 rent). Run by Identity Malta, from 2017 by the Malta Residence and Visa Agency (later Residency Malta Agency). Replaced by the MPRP on 29 Mar 2021; L.N. 122 of 2021 set deadlines for pending applications (end-2021 / 31 Mar 2022). Most applicants were Chinese nationals. ended = closure to new applications.

programs.name: Global Residence Programme (GRP)
programs.notes: Special tax status under the Income Tax Act (L.N. 167 of 2013, S.L. 123.148) for non-EU nationals who buy (EUR 275,000; EUR 220,000 south/Gozo) or rent (EUR 9,600/8,750 a year) property in Malta: 15% tax on foreign income remitted to Malta, minimum EUR 15,000 a year. A tax-residence scheme run by the Commissioner for Revenue rather than an immigration permit, but it lets holders reside in Malta. Succeeded the 2011 High Net Worth Individuals non-EU rules (mlt-hnwi-non-eu). From 1 Jan 2027 the Individual Tax Programme Rules (L.N. 195/2026) apply, with much higher thresholds; existing statuses and applications made by 31 Dec 2026 continue to 31 Dec 2031. No official numbers of beneficiaries or tax collected were found.

programs.name: High Net Worth Individuals - Non-EU/EEA/Swiss Nationals Rules (special tax status)
programs.notes: L.N. 403 of 2011 (S.L. 123.130), deemed in force 1 Jan 2011: 15% tax status for non-EU nationals buying property of at least EUR 400,000 or renting at EUR 20,000 a year, minimum tax EUR 25,000 plus EUR 5,000 per dependant. No applications after 30 Jun 2013 (L.N. 178 of 2013); holders could move to the GRP.

programs.name: Verblijfsregeling vermogende vreemdeling / buitenlandse investeerder (Dutch residence scheme for wealthy foreigners or foreign investors)
programs.notes: Art. 3.29a Vreemdelingenbesluit 2000 (Modern Migration Policy, in force 1 Oct 2013) and Vreemdelingencirculaire B11/2.2: temporary residence permit for investing at least EUR 1,250,000 in an innovative Dutch company or SEED fund, with added value tested by RVO and an FIU check. Fewer than ten permits were ever issued. Abolition decided 11 Jan 2021; abolished from 17 Apr 2024 by Staatsblad 2024, 83 (not 1 Jan 2024). Existing permits keep their validity and can be renewed. Normal naturalisation rules (5 years) apply.

programs.name: Besteuerung nach dem Aufwand / imposition d'après la dépense (Swiss lump-sum taxation)
programs.notes: Not a residence permit but a tax regime (art. 14 DBG and cantonal law) for foreign nationals who take up residence in Switzerland for the first time (or after 10 years away) and do not work there: tax is assessed on worldwide living expenses, with a federal minimum base of CHF 400,000 from 2016 (indexed: CHF 421,700, then CHF 435,000 from 2026) and at least seven times the rent. Abolished in five cantons (ZH, BS, BL, SH, AR); a national abolition initiative failed in 2014. Non-EU nationals need a cantonal permit (che-wealthy-residence-permit). FDK surveys give taxpayer numbers and revenue to 2018. Launch date of this very old regime not established.

programs.name: Aufenthaltsbewilligung wegen erheblicher kantonaler fiskalischer Interessen (Swiss residence permit for wealthy non-working foreigners, art. 30 para. 1(b) AIG / art. 32 VZAE)
programs.notes: Cantons may grant a short-stay or residence permit to protect important public interests, including substantial cantonal fiscal interests (art. 32(1)(c) VZAE); used for wealthy non-EU/EFTA nationals who do not work in Switzerland, typically combined with lump-sum taxation. Each canton sets its own minimum tax expectation; no federal amounts. No official statistics on permits granted on this ground were found.

programs.name: Carte de séjour de résident (Monaco residence card, including for persons of independent means)
programs.notes: Ordonnance Souveraine 3.153 of 1964: a first-time resident card needs housing and either a work permit or proof of sufficient means (art. 6); ordinary 3-year and privileged 10-year cards follow. The law sets no amount; officials and media describe a EUR 500,000 deposit in a Monaco bank as the usual means test for those not working. Not an investment programme in the strict sense, and not specific to non-EU nationals. About 1,300 first-card applications a year (all applicants). launched = date of the ordinance in force.

programs.name: Leidimas laikinai gyventi užsieniečiui, investavusiam į įmonę (Lithuanian temporary residence for company investors, Law on the Legal Status of Aliens art. 45(1)(1), (1¹), (2²))
programs.notes: Temporary residence for a foreign participant or manager of a Lithuanian company: EUR 14,000 own investment in a company with at least EUR 28,000 equity and wage conditions, or EUR 260,000 investment with at least five jobs (added 2016), or managing a company with EUR 500,000 equity and ten jobs. The Commission (2019) dates Lithuania's scheme to 2004 and found no disaggregated statistics. No official counts found. Ordinary naturalisation requires 10 years of residence.

programs.name: Elamisluba ettevõtluseks, sh suurinvestorile (Estonian temporary residence permit for enterprise, including for large investors)
programs.notes: Aliens Act: temporary residence permit for enterprise (EUR 65,000 invested in a company, or EUR 16,000 for a sole proprietor) and, from 18 Jan 2017, for large investors (EUR 1,000,000 directly invested in an Estonian company or fund, no obligation to live in Estonia). Permits up to 5 years, renewable. The Commission dates the Estonian investor scheme to 2009. Three large-investor permits were issued in 2017 (all to Russians). No official series found for later years.

programs.name: Dozvola za boravak i rad za samozapošljavanje (Croatian residence and work permit for self-employed company owners, Zakon o strancima art. 113)
programs.notes: Not a passive investor visa: residence and work permit for a third-country national who owns at least 51% of a company or craft, invested at least EUR 26,544.56 and employs at least three Croatian citizens full-time; key staff of companies with the same capital may also qualify; separate permit for strategic investment projects (art. 115). The Commission (2019) lists Croatia among states with an investor residence scheme (since 2011) and found no statistics. No counts found.

programs.name: Autorisation de séjour pour investisseur (Luxembourg investor residence permit, arts. 53bis-53quater of the immigration law)
programs.notes: Added by the law of 8 March 2017: residence for investing EUR 500,000 in an existing or new Luxembourg company, EUR 3 million in an investment and management structure, or EUR 20 million as a deposit with a Luxembourg financial institution; three-year title after a favourable opinion from the Economy or Finance ministry. Only 9 titles issued (2018-2024), none of the first 7 renewed. Government bill 8586 (21 Jul 2025) would repeal it; still in committee in Sep 2026. status = active until the repeal is adopted.

programs.name: Passeport talent - investisseur économique (French Tech Visa for investors)
programs.notes: Multi-year residence card (up to 4 years) for a foreigner who invests at least EUR 300,000 in France, personally or through a company he runs or owns at least 30% of, creating or saving jobs within four years. Part of the passeport talent created by the law of 7 Mar 2016 (the Commission dates the French scheme to 2016). The Commission reported 29 permits in 2017; no later official breakdown was found.

new_indicators.name: People taxed on a lump-sum (expenditure) basis
new_indicators.definition: Number of taxpayers assessed on their living expenses instead of income and wealth (e.g. Swiss Besteuerung nach dem Aufwand) at a date, usually year-end. A stock.
new_indicators.notes: For tax-residence regimes for wealthy foreigners. Not a count of permits.

new_indicators.name: Tax revenue from lump-sum (expenditure-based) taxation
new_indicators.definition: Tax collected in a period from people taxed on a lump-sum or expenditure basis, all levels of government unless noted.

new_indicators.name: Share of applicants or approved applicants by nationality
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of a programme's applicants (or approved main applicants, as stated in notes) who hold a given nationality, in a period. Use breakdown nationality=ISO3.
new_indicators.notes: Used when sources give only percentages, not counts. Notes must say whether the base is applications or approvals.

gaps: Malta MPRP/MRVP: no Residency Malta Agency annual report or official statistics online; residencymalta.gov.mt (Sucuri) blocks inner pages, and gov.mt press releases and pq.gov.mt parliamentary answers are behind Cloudflare. Approvals by year exist only for 2020-2021 (trade press); no official split by nationality (only shares). MPRP applications in 2023-2025 and approvals 2022-2025 not found.

Malta Global Residence Programme: no official count of beneficiaries or tax collected found (Commissioner for Tax and Customs publishes none we could find); Individual Tax Programme: whether L.N. 195/2026 formally revokes the GRP rules was not confirmed in the text read.
Malta: the Malta Residence Programme (TRP, for EU nationals), Malta Retirement Programme and Nomad Residence Permit were not researched (not investment-based).
Netherlands: only "fewer than ten" permits is published; no exact count, no nationality split, no IND figures on applications.

Switzerland: FDK surveys stop at end-2018 (latest release June 2019); the 2022 national figure (3,478) is from Blick, which cites unspecified federal data. No statistics on art. 32 VZAE "fiscal interest" permits for non-EU nationals (SEM) were found. Canton-level tables in the FDK release were not transcribed (breakdown key for cantons does not exist). The official 2014 vote result page (bk.admin.ch) could not be captured; the result is from Swissvotes.
Monaco: no official statistics on residence cards issued (IMSEE Monaco en Chiffres download timed out); the EUR 500,000 bank-deposit requirement is described only in media, not in the ordinance.
Lithuania: Migration Department yearbooks were not checked for permits under art. 45(1)(1¹); entry-into-force dates of amounts not established.
Estonia: PPA statistics on large-investor and enterprise permits after 2017 not found; the meaning of the Commission's Estonian series 2012-2017 (61, 54, 35, 28, 18, 68) is unclear.
Croatia: no investor-specific scheme beyond the self-employment/business permit; no counts found.

Slovenia: no investor residence route found in the Aliens Act (ZTuj-2) beyond ordinary business and self-employment permits; the Commission (2019) did not list Slovenia among states with investor residence schemes. No programme row created.
Luxembourg: the 2019 parliamentary answer (six investors) was read only via Paperjam; the original law of 8 March 2017 was not downloaded (Legilux URLs not resolved).
France: no official yearly count of passeport talent investor cards found after 2017; CESEDA article numbers not verified on Légifrance.

Not covered for lack of time or search budget: Andorra (passive residence with investment), San Marino, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Romania, Poland, Austria (private-means settlement permit), Serbia/Montenegro property residence.
